title: Quiet anchor & steady-drift notebook
content:
Purpose:
- Lightweight personal playbook for quiet/steady drift rollouts where we avoid big cohort jumps. Focus is on an anchor cohort that keeps a stable behavioral baseline while we slowly diffuse traffic to new model/version.

High-level idea (one-liner):
- Anchor a small set of clients (the anchor) to old stable variant, let drift happen around them with slow diffusion to new variant; use telemetry-driven micro-adjustments instead of big flips.

Anchor definition & selection criteria:
- Size: 8–12 client keys (tenant IDs) that are low-churn and representative. Prefer long-lived customers with broad prompt patterns.
- Eligibility: <2% monthly config changes, stable usage (coefficient of variation < 0.25), opt-in beta partners if needed.
- Affinity: Prefer clients using the product surface with medium latency sensitivity (chat, autocomplete). Exclude short-burst telemetry-heavy jobs.

Sequence (template):
1) Preflight (T-72h):
   - Validate image & quantization artifacts in staging.
   - Run 1k synthetic prompts through model in staging to exercise long-tail sequences (max seq 2048).
   - Generate expected cache keys for anchor prompts to prewarm caches (see cache-priming section).
   - Confirm canary instance sizes and autoscale policies.

2) Anchor activation (T-24h):
   - Pin anchor cohort to stable variant-1 at 100%.
   - Observe baseline metrics for 12–24h: p50/p95 latency, token throughput, error rate, gpu utilization, tail queues.

3) Quiet diffusion (T+0 onward):
   - Deploy new variant behind routing layer but assign only 0.5% of non-anchor traffic initially.
   - Ramp non-anchor fraction on an exponential slow curve: 0.5% -> 1% -> 2% -> 4% -> 8% over ~48–72h depending on signals.
   - Every step: hold for 2–6h minimum and evaluate.

4) Steady drift checks (continuous):
   - Compare new variant vs anchor baseline for: response correctness (sample evals), p95 latency, error spike signals, token distribution drift, hallucination flag rate (from quality monitor).
   - If any safety gate trips, pause ramp and execute mitigation (throttle new variant to last safe fraction or roll back).

5) Unpin & folding (T+7d typical):
   - If steady state and quality signals stable for 48–72h at target fraction: gradually unpin anchor (reduce anchor fraction by 10% per 12h).
   - Alternatively: convert anchor to shadowing only and allow auto-routing to converge.

Cache-priming checklist (notes):
- For anchor prompts: collect 200 representative recent prompts per anchor client; push them to prewarm job that populates KV caches and consecutive prefix states.
- For LRU eviction risk: run prewarm within 1–4h before release so caches are hot when traffic arrives.
- If quantized model changes KV layout: include synthetic warmup that does full attention/kv state reuse — not just single-shot prompts.

Telemetry & safety gates (numbers are my working thresholds — tune per-service):
- Latency: p95 increase > 20% relative to anchor baseline -> pause and evaluate.
- Errors: absolute error rate delta > 0.4% or relative > 2x -> pause.
- GPU health: sustained util > 88% for 15+ minutes or memory growth trends indicating leaks -> alert SRE and pause new traffic.
- Token drop / truncation events: any unexplained rise -> investigate immediately.
- Quality signals: automated eval score drop > 3 points (on our internal 100pt scale) against anchor prompt set -> halt ramp.
- Observability sanity: missing traces or partial sampling in span -> treat as high risk.

Runbooks / quick actions (cheat-sheet):
- Pause ramp: set routing fraction to last safe value; set flag in release dashboard.
- Re-pin anchor full: if multiple signals active, pin anchor back to 100% until root cause identified.
- Hotfix path: hotpatch model config (smaller token cap, disable sampling temperature changes) and re-run small test before resuming.
- Emergency rollback: execute image switch to previous artifact and schedule postmortem.

Unknowns / open questions (todo):
- How many anchor clients are ideal for multi-region footprints? (E.g., 3 anchors per region?) Needs experiment.
- Can we automate cache-priming generation from 10% of real traffic without exposing customer PII? Need PM/security input.
- Should anchors be billed/credited differently? commercial asks might surface.

Notes-to-self (short fragments):
- Try a 5-day drift vs 48h; longer tends to surface more semantic regressions but costs more monitoring overhead.
- Build a small dashboard widget that computes rolling baseline deltas for each anchor (delta p95, delta eval_score).
- Consider an ‘anchor aging’ signal: if anchor behavior drifts > X% vs population for > 7 days, rotate anchor client.

Mini experiment plan (A/B within quiet-drift):
- Hypothesis: slow diffusion with anchor reduces rollback frequency by 30% vs direct 10% canary.
- Metric: rollback count within 7 days, avg time-to-detect, percent of total downtime attributable to model behavior.
- Experiment groups: 
   A: Quiet-anchor pattern (this doc) across 20 releases (N=20).
   B: Standard canary (10% canary, 2-step ramp) across 20 releases.
- Collect telemetry and compare.

Reference shortcuts (tickets & reading):
- CON-2382: Anchor cohort selection criteria (proto).
- JIRA-RELEASE-492: Last warmup chore for quantized kernels.
- Slack: #runtime-ops pinned thread "quiet-rollouts" for postmortem snippets.

Quick checklist before calling a release 'stable':
- 72h at target traffic fraction with anchor pinned and no safety gate trips.
- Quality evals on 500 anchor prompts: no more than 1.5% regression in key metrics.
- No memory / GPU leakage signals for 48h.
- All observability spans present and sampling >= 2% on tail traces.
- Stakeholder thumbs-up (prod-eng, SRE, QA).

Signature / micro-retrospective: 
- If this routine causes frequent pausing at the 2% stage, iterate with smaller anchor or longer holds.
- Keep notes here after each release — short bullet lines with date + what happened.

Recent entries (quick log):
- 2025-02-20: Dry-run on staging looked fine. Prewarm tightened cache hit-rate by ~7pp.
- 2025-02-25: Live ramp to 4% paused due to p95 spike (22%); investigation pointed to a kernel scheduling change. Rolled back to 1% pending kernel fix.
- 2025-02-28: Kernel fix deployed; resumed slow ramp, anchor held steady.

End of notebook — will copy useful bits into confluence playbook once stable pattern emerges.

-- Micah
